name: The President

location.address: Congress Trail, Giant Forest, Sequoia National Park, Tulare County, California
location.neighbourhood: Giant Forest, on the Congress Trail loop, reached from the Sherman Tree parking lot

access: Paid entry (Sequoia National Park entrance fee); on the paved Congress Trail loop, reached from the Sherman Tree parking lot near General Sherman.
transport: No public transit; nearest town Three Rivers, CA, about 45 minutes' drive from the park entrance.
verify_notes: Second-largest tree on Earth by overall volume (trunk plus branches, ~1,278 m3 trunk + ~255 m3 branches per Wikipedia); by trunk volume alone it ranks lower, which some sources report as 4th largest. Named 1923 for President Warren G. Harding. Widely reported (Wikipedia) as the oldest known living giant sequoia at roughly 3,240 years, dated via extensive 2011-12 measurement campaign (photogrammetry, referenced by NPS's largest-trees-in-world page). Dense crown, prominent white burn scar on north side, first large branch at 37m. Stands 140 ft downhill/below Chief Sequoyah Tree on the same trail loop. Coordinates from Wikipedia infobox (36.57341,-118.75010), close to but distinct from an independent Wikidata sweep figure (36.56250,-118.75139) which was not used as it could not be corroborated; Wikipedia's figure is the one matching the described location relative to Chief Sequoyah and General Sherman.

name: Chief Sequoyah Tree

location.address: Congress Trail, Giant Forest, Sequoia National Park, Tulare County, California
location.neighbourhood: Giant Forest, on the Congress Trail loop, about 140 feet uphill from the President Tree

access: Paid entry (Sequoia National Park entrance fee); on the paved Congress Trail loop.
transport: No public transit; nearest town Three Rivers, CA, about 45 minutes' drive from the park entrance.
verify_notes: 9th largest tree in Giant Forest grove, 27th largest giant sequoia in the world by one count (Wikipedia) / ranked #30 by another source (Sequoia Quest); minor disagreement on exact rank, not on scale. Named 1928 by park superintendent Colonel John R. White for Sequoyah, the Cherokee polymath who created the Cherokee syllabary in 1821 (Sequoia Quest gives 1926; Wikipedia gives 1928, flagging the year discrepancy). Enormous burl on its southern face, fire scarring on the western face. No age estimate found in either source and no girth-based derivation attempted here (no cited growth-rate basis); flag as unknown and let the page ask.

name: Lincoln Tree

location.address: Giant Forest, Sequoia National Park, Tulare County, California
location.neighbourhood: Giant Forest grove, near the Congress Trail loop

access: Paid entry (Sequoia National Park entrance fee); Giant Forest grove, reached from the Congress Trail area near General Sherman.
transport: No public transit; nearest town Three Rivers, CA, about 45 minutes' drive from the park entrance.
verify_notes: Widely reported as the fourth largest tree on Earth by volume, though volume estimates vary between sources: Wendell Flint calculated 44,471 cubic feet, while earlier White and Pusateri measurements gave 51,000 cubic feet (Wikipedia notes the disagreement). Irregular base with prominent burn scars on north, south and west faces, plus a white burl on the northeast face and a bleached, broad-branched top. No age estimate found in either source; girth here is base circumference (98.5 ft = 30.1m) converted to cm.

name: Franklin Tree

location.address: Giant Forest, Sequoia National Park, Tulare County, California
location.neighbourhood: Giant Forest grove, near the Washington Tree

access: Paid entry (Sequoia National Park entrance fee); Giant Forest grove.
transport: No public transit; nearest town Three Rivers, CA, about 45 minutes' drive from the park entrance.
verify_notes: Eighth largest giant sequoia in the world (Wikipedia), named by dendrologist Wendell Flint for Benjamin Franklin. Its size went unrecognised until Flint's 1950s measurement campaign, likely overlooked earlier due to its proximity to the much larger Washington Tree. Elevation over 1,800m. Neither source fetched gives exact GPS coordinates or trail distance; the coordinate here is from a Wikidata sweep (not independently corroborated), so location_precision is approximate pending a tree-level source. No age estimate found.

name: Washington Tree

location.address: Giant Forest, Sequoia National Park, Tulare County, California
location.neighbourhood: Giant Forest grove, near the Franklin Tree

access: Paid entry (Sequoia National Park entrance fee); Giant Forest grove.
transport: No public transit; nearest town Three Rivers, CA, about 45 minutes' drive from the park entrance.
verify_notes: ALIVE, confirmed by both sources: a lightning-strike fire (dated September 2003 by Wikipedia, September 2002 by Sequoia Quest; flagging the year disagreement, not the fact of the strike) reduced its crown, then a heavy snow load in January 2005 collapsed its upper half, cutting its height from about 253.7 ft (77.3m) to roughly 115-123 ft (35-37m), over half its original height, and hollowing the remaining upper trunk. Both sources independently report new foliage/small branches growing back on the south side since, meaning it survives and has been reinstated on largest-trees lists (around #55, well down from its former #2 ranking). This is a genuinely worthwhile entry for the story of near-total collapse and continued survival, not merely a stump. Original pre-damage volume was 49,550 cubic feet, second largest known at the time; current remaining volume estimated at just over 30,000 cubic feet including hollows. No age estimate found in either source. Girth here is DERIVED (pi times Wikipedia's pre-damage 29.9ft basal diameter = 2862cm), not a directly reported circumference; no separate post-collapse girth measurement was found in either source, so flagged.
